rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem scopes the item explicitly to the baseline assessment and restates the cue cluster. Baseline supplies every element: known T6 and T8 osseous metastases, escalating band-like mid-thoracic pain no longer relieved by oxycodone, 4/5 and 4-minus/5 lower-extremity weakness with hyperreflexia and an extensor left plantar response, a T8 sensory level with a T6-T7 hyperaesthetic band, diminished rectal tone, and a post-void residual of 280 mL. That combination is malignant spinal cord compression, and the corrected calcium of 10.1 and the intact orientation exclude the hypercalcaemia and neurotoxicity alternatives.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 confirms the diagnosis by MRI; it is not needed, since the clinical syndrome is complete at baseline. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The option set names the four candidate actions, and the prioritisation is oncologic-emergency knowledge: high-dose corticosteroid is the time-critical intervention that limits cord oedema, ahead of a full head-to-toe assessment, catheter preparation or reassurance. Baseline already establishes the compression syndrome with a T8 sensory level, hyperreflexia, an upgoing left toe and a 280 mL residual, so the urgency is visible without a stage.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 must not be the boundary: it records the provider ordering 'an immediate increase of dexamethasone to 10 mg IV bolus now... (urgent MSCC dexamethasone protocol)', whose wording flags the keyed action as the urgent one. Recorded qualifier: the keyed option reads 'as prescribed' and that prescription is written in stage_1, but the action is correct on knowledge and the option supplies its own premise. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates both findings - a bladder scan of 420 mL and new perineal numbness - and baseline supplies the comparator and the anatomy: a post-void residual of 280 mL on admission, a T8 sensory level with diminished rectal tone, and epidural metastatic disease at T6 and T8. Rising retention with saddle numbness is autonomic and sacral involvement from progressive cord compression, not infection, opioid effect or dehydration.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 is the source of the two findings the stem restates, and it offers no interpretation. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the premise that emergent decompression is recommended, and baseline supplies the one case-specific element the keyed set depends on: enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneous daily on the home medication list, which must be held and communicated before spinal surgery. Verifying surgeon-obtained informed consent, ensuring current laboratories with a type and screen and imaging, and continuing serial neurological assessments are standard preoperative practice, while the nurse explaining surgical risks and prognosis, and driving glucose to 100 with stat insulin, both fall outside scope or safety.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 carries the surgical recommendation the stem restates and the steroid hyperglycaemia that one distractor exploits; it states no preparation set. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem quotes the daughter's question, and baseline supplies what an honest answer must hold together: metastatic disease with cord compression, and preserved though reduced lower-extremity movement. The keyed response acknowledges the fear, states the surgical goal as decompression and prevention of further loss, notes preserved movement as encouraging without promising recovery, and refers prognosis to the neurosurgeon; the alternatives promise ambulation, declare permanent damage, or refuse to engage.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 carries the question the stem restates; it states no response. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The column is labelled 'Improvement from Stage 2 Preoperative Status' but neither the rows nor the columns state the Stage 2 values, and against BASELINE two keyed rows invert. Baseline records lower-extremity strength of 4/5 with 4-minus/5 dorsiflexion and a sensory level at T8; the postoperative row of 3/5 strength would therefore read as a decline rather than an improvement, and the row of a T8-T9 sensory level would read as unchanged. Both become improvements only against stage_2, where strength had fallen to 2/5 with dorsiflexion 1/5 on the left and the sensory level had risen to T6. stage_2 is the earliest boundary at which the comparator the item names actually exists.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 supplies the preoperative comparator without classifying anything; it is the record of deterioration, not of response. stage_3 must not be the boundary: its narrative annotates the findings for the learner, stating that strength is 'improved from the 2 out of 5 seen preoperatively', that dorsiflexion is 'improved on the left from 1 out of 5', and that 'Sensory level has improved', which hands over the keyed classification for three of the four rows.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem scopes the item explicitly to the initial assessment and baseline laboratory data before Stage 1 begins, so the boundary is settled by the stem itself. Baseline supplies the decisive values - troponin I 0.18 against a normal below 0.04, BNP 245, AST 88 and ALT 112, CRP 3.8 - alongside new exertional chest heaviness, resting tachycardia at 102 and right-upper-quadrant tenderness. Holding the scheduled checkpoint-inhibitor infusion and notifying the oncologist immediately follows; proceeding, treating nausea first, or deferring to routine rounds do not.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 narrates the nurse doing exactly this - reviewing the labs, noting the elevations in context, and the oncologist placing the infusion on hold - which is the keyed action carried out. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Baseline already contains the full constellation: a cardiac signal in troponin 0.18 with BNP 245, chest heaviness and sinus tachycardia, a hepatic signal in AST 88 with ALT 112 and right-upper-quadrant tenderness, a systemic inflammatory CRP of 3.8, and a prior immune-mediated rash on checkpoint-inhibitor therapy. Two concurrent organ-specific immune toxicities is what distinguishes the keyed hypothesis from isolated viral myocarditis, plaque-rupture coronary syndrome, and metastatic progression, and baseline's normal PR interval and clear lungs argue against the alternatives.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 assembles the same list for the learner - 'the elevated troponin I, BNP, AST, ALT, and CRP in the context of new-onset exertional chest heaviness and resting tachycardia' - and adds a new first-degree block, which confirms rather than establishes the hypothesis. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the situation, haemodynamic deterioration with urgent orders received, and the option set names the four actions. Sequencing oxygen for the breathing deficit, then telemetry and reliable access, then the high-dose methylprednisolone that treats the underlying immune myocarditis, then transfer to higher acuity is prioritisation knowledge. Baseline supplies the myocarditis picture that makes the steroid the definitive step.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 is where the deterioration and orders occur, which the stem restates; it states no sequence. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the premise, monitoring after corticosteroid administration, and baseline supplies the two organ systems to trend - troponin with BNP for the cardiac toxicity and transaminases for the hepatic toxicity - plus a normal baseline glucose of 104 that makes steroid-induced hyperglycaemia a new risk. Serial biomarkers, four-to-six-hourly glucose, continuous telemetry with arrhythmia and conduction alarms, and assessment for overlapping myositis or myasthenic features are indicated, while stopping cardiac monitoring once the PR interval normalises is not.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3 reports the response to steroids including a rising glucose; it states no monitoring plan. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the order itself - permanent discontinuation of all checkpoint-inhibitor therapy - and the answer is medication-order scope: verify the discontinuation in the administration record per the provider order, document the adverse drug reaction, and educate the patient about the permanence. Recording it as a temporary hold, deleting the order independently, or requesting a switch to single-agent therapy each exceed or contradict nursing scope.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 carries the order the stem restates; it states no nursing action. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Each row states its own finding, including the troponin row that carries both endpoints of the fall from 1.42 to 0.64, and baseline supplies the pre-treatment glucose of 104 that makes 218 a treatment-related effect rather than a pre-existing abnormality. rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: All four options state their own findings - worsening hypotension despite the fluid bolus, oliguria of 30 mL over two hours, new erythema extending 2 cm without purulent drainage, and shivering with rigors after antibiotic and electrolyte administration - so the competing explanations and their evidence are inside the part. rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states both decisive values - a blood glucose of 324 rising despite sliding-scale coverage, with parenteral nutrition continuing at 85 mL/hr - and baseline establishes the continuous dextrose load. Notifying the provider and anticipating a continuous insulin infusion with a possible rate reduction is the scope-appropriate action, while independently stopping or pausing the infusion risks rebound hypoglycaemia and continuing unchanged ignores the trend.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1 is the source of the glucose value the stem restates; it states no action. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the finding and its interpretation in full, including the differential-time-to-positivity caveat, and the option set names the four coordination steps. Sequencing provider communication, verification that empiric coverage is infusing, coordination for alternative access and glycaemic management, and then line removal under orders is catheter-infection management logic. Baseline supplies the parenteral-nutrition dependence that makes alternative access a prerequisite to removal.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the whole problem - no mouth rinses for over six hours because of severe pain from confluent bleeding mucositis, with the patient refusing further attempts - and baseline establishes the mucositis and the analgesia available. Timing analgesia fifteen to twenty minutes before assisting with atraumatic sodium bicarbonate rinses respects both the oral-care need and the pain; a standard toothbrush, forceful lemon-glycerin swabbing and indefinite deferral all fail on mucosal safety or on abandoning care.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2 is the source of the situation the stem restates; it prescribes no intervention. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Each row states its own finding, and two carry their own trend endpoints - lactate falling from 3.6 to 1.9 and temperature falling from 102.9 F to 100.6 F. rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the Stage 3 status it asks about - the patient tolerates gentle mouth rinses with coaching but cannot swallow liquids - and baseline establishes grade-level mucositis with parenteral nutrition as the delivery route. Recognising that tolerating a rinse is not equivalent to tolerating nutritional intake, and that severe systemic inflammation with severe mucositis does not yet permit an enteral transition, is nutrition-support knowledge; the line-patency and infection-risk rationales in the other options do not govern the decision.
